issues.claim: price_ranges.low_cost_self_serve: "$0-$45 per month of software, or $149-$250 one-time hardware"
issues.problem: Unit/term mismatch in a range endpoint. The $45 figure is Monnit's iMonnit Premiere 6-sensor license at $45.00 PER YEAR (Monnit product page shows $45.00; the vendor support article calls Premiere a "paid yearly subscription ... starts at $45/year"), yet it is used as the top of a PER MONTH band. No source in the brief shows a $45/month software price. The brief's own inference_note even labels it "$45.00/year", so the narrative and the range header disagree, and the top of the band does not follow from the sourced prices.
issues.fix: Restate the low band as sourced: "$0-$35/month of software (ThermoWorks Free/Home/Pro/Business Pro) or $29 hub + $8 per sensor per month (Zip); Monnit Premiere is $45-$325 per year, i.e. about $3.75-$27/month". If a $45/month top is wanted, cite Zip at $29 + 2 x $8 = $45/month and say so.

issues.claim: price_ranges.inference_note ("a New Jersey contractor's stated typical project range"), implications_for_consultancy[1] ("a $1,200-$8,000 typical installed range from an NJ refrigeration firm") and one_line ("a New Jersey contractor quoting a typical installed job at $1,200-$8,000")
issues.problem: The price itself is confirmed ($1,200-$8,000, "typical range, not a quote"), but the attribution is misstated. The cited page (tomsrivercommercialrefrigeration.com) labels itself in its own header: "Ocean County, New Jersey Commercial refrigeration ... Referral service — not a contractor". The brief's own buyer_reported_costs entry correctly says "site is a referral service, not the installing contractor", so the document contradicts itself and the ranges/implications upgrade a lead-generation site's estimate into a contractor quote.
issues.fix: Use one description everywhere: "an Ocean County, NJ refrigeration referral/lead-generation site's stated typical project range of $1,200-$8,000 (explicitly 'not a quote', not an installing contractor's price)".

issues.claim: price_ranges.mid_market: "$77-$210 per location per month (about $10-$21 per monitored unit plus a $29-$150 platform fee)"
issues.problem: The $77 endpoint does not decompose on the stated per-unit band. Per the inference_note, $77 = Zip at six sensors ($29 + 6 x $8), but $8/sensor is below the stated $10 per-unit floor, so the range header and its own derivation use different unit rates ($8 vs $10-$21). $210 does follow ($150 + 6 x $10, ConnectedFresh's own 4-6 unit figure).
issues.fix: Either lower the per-unit floor to "$8-$21 per monitored unit" and say the $77 endpoint is Zip at six sensors, or keep the $10 floor and state the $77 endpoint as a Zip configuration at 4 sensors plus a rate inside the band, noting it is not Zip's six-sensor arithmetic.

issues.claim: one_line: "small metered subscriptions ($0-$45 per month, or $5-$21 per sensor per month mid-market)"
issues.problem: Internal inconsistency: price_ranges describes the $5-$21 per-sensor-per-month figure as the equivalent of the LOW-cost band ("$149-$250 one-time hardware, equivalent to roughly $5-$21 per sensor per month"), while the one-liner places $5-$21 per sensor under mid-market. The $0-$45/month figure also carries the annual-vs-monthly problem noted above.
issues.fix: Make the one-liner match price_ranges: keep $5-$21 per sensor per month in the low/self-serve band and give mid-market its own $10-$21 per monitored unit plus platform-fee wording, or vice versa, but do not use the same $5-$21 band for both.

issues.claim: buyer_reported_costs: Jolt figures sourced to softwarefinder.com labelled year "2026"
issues.problem: The numbers are confirmed verbatim ($89.99/month/location baseline, $296/month + $549 setup negotiated to $207.75, four locations about $664.80/month total, about $149.58/location/month on annual billing), but the page carries no publication or update date, so "2026" is an assumption (retrieval year), not something the source states.
issues.fix: Change the year to "Undated third-party pricing guide; retrieved 2026-11-12" (the other buyer_reported entries already handle undated pages this way).

issues.claim: buyer_complaints: "Temp Stick monitors ambient air only, cannot be recalibrated (only offset in settings)" cited to https://tempstick.com/common-questions/
issues.problem: The substance is confirmed on Ideal Sciences' own site, but not at the cited URL: fetching /common-questions/ did not surface the calibration or ambient-air passage, and a text search of the fetched page found no match for 'calibrat', 'ambient', 'offset', 'probe' or 'factory'. The vendor's help article https://tempstick.com/help/calibrate-temperature-humidity/ does state the unit arrives factory-calibrated and that users only add an offset in the app.
issues.fix: Cite https://tempstick.com/help/calibrate-temperature-humidity/ (plus a product-page line that the classic sensor measures air temperature, not food temperature) instead of /common-questions/.
